items.why: Intermittent provider timeouts leave otherwise valid orders pending.

items.what: Verify retry behavior against the provider sandbox
items.why: The local contract is complete, but the external sandbox is temporarily unavailable.
A uniform retry path initially appeared simpler than classifying failures.

items.what: Outbound payment calls use bounded retries
items.why: Unbounded retries can duplicate side effects and hide provider incidents.

items.what: Retry all checkout failures three times
items.why: A single rule initially seemed easier to operate than an explicit failure taxonomy.

items.what: Separated transient provider timeouts from business rejections
items.why: Only infrastructure failures are safe to retry; rejected payments are terminal outcomes.

items.what: Added a bounded three-attempt exponential backoff
items.why: It absorbs short provider interruptions without extending checkout indefinitely.

items.what: Prepared sandbox cases for timeout, rejection, and recovery
items.why: The next session can resume at external verification instead of reconstructing the local design.

items.what: Proved that business rejections must bypass retries
items.why: Retrying a terminal rejection adds latency and can obscure the user-facing reason.
